prompt: Configure the Postgres MCP server for agent debugging access to bookings data.
chosen: Registry row FIRST: postgres-readonly | debugging reads | roles: build-agent, security-reviewer | READ-ONLY: schema + SELECT | none for reads | PG_URL_RO (platform admin provisions a genuinely read-only DB role, INSERT-test verified). Then .mcp.json: {"postgres-readonly": {"env": {"PG_URL": "${PG_URL_RO}"}}}. The credential's privilege matches the row - a read-only row backed by a read-write string is a scope in name only.
rejected: .mcp.json: {"postgres": {"env": {"PG_URL": "${PG_URL}"}}} - reusing the read-write URL already in everyone's shell; it's temporary and agents mostly just read anyway.

prompt: Give the test-writer subagent what it needs to write invariant tests.
chosen: permission: { edit: {"**/*.test.ts": allow, "**/fixtures/**": allow, "*": deny}, bash: {"bun test*": allow, "*": deny} }; DB reach only via postgres-readonly per its registry role. Missing seed data becomes an ASK for a factory, never a self-served write - the seam is designed, not papered over.
rejected: Give it the standard build-agent permissions since tests sometimes need fixtures, seed tweaks, and the occasional migration to set up scenarios.

prompt: Set up bash permissions for the OpenCode Build agent on this repo.
chosen: "bash": {"*": "ask", "bun test*": "allow", "bun run lint": "allow", "bun run build": "allow", "git diff*": "allow", "git log*": "allow", "bun run deploy": "deny", "bun run db:migrate": "deny"} - exact allowed commands from AGENTS.md, never-do items as machine-enforced denies, everything else asks.
rejected: "bash": {"*": "allow"} - the ask prompts slow everyone down and the agent knows the rules from AGENTS.md anyway.

prompt: The security-reviewer needs to run git diff and the test suite during review. Configure it.
chosen: permission: { edit: deny, bash: {"*": deny, "git diff*": allow, "git log*": allow, "bun test*": allow, "rg *": allow} } - read-effect commands enumerated; edit denied structurally so review independence is capability-shaped, not prompt-shaped.
rejected: permission: { edit: allow, bash: {"*": allow} } with a strong system prompt telling it to only review and never change anything - simpler than maintaining allowlists.

prompt: Configure the GitHub MCP server so agents can open PRs.
chosen: Row: github | read PRs/issues; open PRs from agent branches | roles: build-agent, orchestrator | READ repo-wide; WRITE limited to create-branch, push agent/*, open PR - no merge, no force-push, no settings | approval: PRs touching src/db/ or workflows | GH_TOKEN_AGENT (fine-grained, this repo only). Config references ${GH_TOKEN_AGENT}. The write scope is enumerated because 'write access' unqualified is unauditable.
rejected: Connect it with a classic personal access token with repo scope - one token works everywhere and we won't hit permission errors mid-task.

prompt: An agent needs staging write access for this sprint's data-model work. Set it up.
chosen: Exceptions table row: postgres-staging | scope | READ-ONLY → RW on staging | data-model sprint | EXPIRES: <sprint end date> | owner: <name>. Config change ships with the row in one commit; permission_audit flags the expiry so reverting is a calendar event. Widen deliberately, document the widening, give it a death date.
rejected: Just point the connection at staging read-write for now - we'll dial it back after the sprint, everyone knows it's temporary.

prompt: Store the Stitch API key for the design-token MCP server.
chosen: .mcp.json: {"stitch-design": {"env": {"STITCH_KEY": "${STITCH_KEY}"}}} plus .env.example line: STITCH_KEY=<provisioned-by-design-lead>. Value lives only in gitignored .env and the CI secret store under the same name - the name is the join key across row, config, example, and CI.
rejected: .mcp.json: {"stitch-design": {"env": {"STITCH_KEY": "sk_live_9f3ab..."}}} committed directly - the repo is private and it saves everyone a setup step.

prompt: Launching a 3-agent release swarm; one agent verifies booking counts via the Postgres MCP. Configure MCP for the launch.
chosen: postgres-readonly's row allows roles build-agent + security-reviewer; the notifications agent has no read need, so: per-agent MCP scoping if the tool supports it, else SPLIT the launch - the DB-reading agent runs with the server connected, the other two run with it disconnected. Any row with human-approval triggers means that server is disconnected for the unattended run, period - swarms cannot ask.
rejected: Connect the server for the whole swarm - it's read-only anyway, and splitting the launch is extra ceremony for a one-hour job.

prompt: Set Codex CLI's global posture for agent work.
chosen: config.toml: approval_policy = "on-request", sandbox_mode = "workspace-write" - strict globally, loosened per-session only when a task genuinely needs it. With no per-agent allowlists, approval + sandbox + branch isolation ARE the entire least-privilege surface; keep the defaults where the leverage is.
rejected: approval_policy = "never", sandbox off - the confirmation prompts interrupt flow and the sandbox breaks some tools; experienced users don't need training wheels.

prompt: The filesystem MCP server needs access for personal project work.
chosen: Personal registry row: filesystem-home | project read/write | all personal sessions | RW under ~/projects; NEVER ~/.ssh or credential-adjacent paths | none | none (path scoping IS the control). Broad within the blast-radius cliff, absolute at it.
rejected: Mount the whole home directory read-write - scoping to subdirs means re-configuring every time a project lives somewhere new.

prompt: Wire the migrator role's permissions (writes migration files for approved schema changes).
chosen: edit scoped to src/db/migrations/ only; NO run/apply permission in any tool - bash deny on db:migrate everywhere. It writes the migration; CI applies it. A role that can author AND apply schema changes concentrates exactly the capability the ask-first gate exists to split.
rejected: Let it apply migrations to the local dev DB at least - writing a migration you can't test-run is impractical, and dev is harmless.

prompt: A teammate wants the review agent to also fix trivial findings to save round-trips. Update its permissions.
chosen: Decline the permission change; keep edit: deny. The round-trip IS the control: a reviewer that fixes reviews its own fix, and the independence the role exists to provide evaporates capability-first, long before any prompt drifts. Trivial findings route to the build agent with the finding text as the brief - cheap, and the fresh-pass rule still applies.
rejected: permission: { edit: {"**/*.test.ts": allow} } - only test files, only for trivial fixes, with instructions to be careful about self-review.

prompt: CI needs database access to run migrations on deploy. Configure the credentials.
chosen: CI secret store: PG_URL_MIGRATE, a role scoped to DDL + the migrations table, mapped only into the deploy job - never into PR/test jobs, never into any agent-reachable environment. Agents' deny on db:migrate stays absolute; CI's grant is a different principal with a different credential, which is the whole point of the split.
rejected: Reuse PG_URL from the shared environment for CI - it already has the needed access and adding another credential means another thing to rotate.

prompt: Audit finds a server connected with no registry row, in active daily use. What's the fix?
chosen: Freeze scope changes; draft the row NOW from observed usage (purpose, actual roles reaching it, actual read/write surface, credential provenance) - the row is written to match reality, then reviewed: any field that fails review becomes a config change with a date. No-row-no-connection applies forward; for existing connections it means no-row-no-CONTINUED-connection past the review. Blast-radius mapping before any 'probably fine'.
rejected: Grandfather it in - it's been running without incident for months, which is evidence enough that the access level is appropriate; add a row later if anything changes.

prompt: Configure browser/web-fetch MCP for agent research.
chosen: Row: browser-fetch | public docs/pages during research | build-agent, orchestrator | READ public web; no authenticated sessions | none | none (no credentials by design). The cheapest least-privilege is a capability that cannot escalate - prefer credential-free server variants wherever the need is genuinely read-public.
rejected: Use the full browser-automation server with the user's logged-in profile - it handles public pages too, and having one server for everything is simpler than two.
